entries.text: Mercury. The speedy little planet. Find the tiny grey planet racing closest to the Sun.
Smallest planet in our solar system.
Discovery 1. Smallest planet in our solar system.
Closest to the Sun and very speedy.
Discovery 2. Closest to the Sun and very speedy.
From one sunrise to the next takes 176 Earth days.
Discovery 3. From one sunrise to the next takes 176 Earth days.
No air to breathe, so it is quiet.
Discovery 4. No air to breathe, so it is quiet.
Long cliffs formed as Mercury cooled and shrank.
Discovery 5. Long cliffs formed as Mercury cooled and shrank.
Temperatures swing from baking hot to freezing cold.
Discovery 6. Temperatures swing from baking hot to freezing cold.
Correct. It has no air.
Venus. The hottest planet. Spot the yellow world hidden beneath thick clouds.
Hottest planet in the whole solar system.
Discovery 1. Hottest planet in the whole solar system.
Spins backwards compared to most planets.
Discovery 2. Spins backwards compared to most planets.
Thick clouds trap heat like a blanket.
Discovery 3. Thick clouds trap heat like a blanket.
Looks like a bright evening star.
Discovery 4. Looks like a bright evening star.
Its clouds contain drops of strong acid.
Discovery 5. Its clouds contain drops of strong acid.
The Sun rises in the west because Venus spins backwards.
Discovery 6. The Sun rises in the west because Venus spins backwards.
Correct. Venus.
Earth. Our bright blue home. Find the blue oceans that cover most of Earth.
Home to plants, animals, and you!
Discovery 1. Home to plants, animals, and you!
Lots of water makes it look blue.
Discovery 2. Lots of water makes it look blue.
Only planet we know with life.
Discovery 3. Only planet we know with life.
One big Moon lights up our night sky.
Discovery 4. One big Moon lights up our night sky.
Earth’s moving plates slowly reshape its surface.
Discovery 5. Earth’s moving plates slowly reshape its surface.
Earth acts like a giant magnet. Its invisible magnetic field turns many tiny bits from the Sun away from Earth. The space around Earth that the field controls is called the magnetosphere.

Discovery 6. Earth acts like a giant magnet. Its invisible magnetic field turns many tiny bits from the Sun away from Earth. The space around Earth that the field controls is called the magnetosphere.
Correct. Its oceans.
Mars. The red explorer. Search the red surface for the giant Olympus Mons volcano.
Dusty and rocky with huge volcanoes.
Discovery 1. Dusty and rocky with huge volcanoes.
Robots explore Mars for us!
Discovery 2. Robots explore Mars for us!
Home to the biggest volcano: Olympus Mons.
Discovery 3. Home to the biggest volcano: Olympus Mons.
Looks red because of rusty dust.
Discovery 4. Looks red because of rusty dust.
Olympus Mons is nearly three times taller than Everest.
Discovery 5. Olympus Mons is nearly three times taller than Everest.
Mars has seasons and polar ice caps like Earth.
Discovery 6. Mars has seasons and polar ice caps like Earth.
Correct. Rusty dust.
Jupiter. The giant gas planet. Find the striped giant and its enormous red storm.
Largest planet in our solar system.
Discovery 1. Largest planet in our solar system.
Bigger than all the other planets combined.
Discovery 2. Bigger than all the other planets combined.
Has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot.
Discovery 3. Has a giant storm called the Great Red Spot.
Made of gas, so there is no solid ground.
Discovery 4. Made of gas, so there is no solid ground.
Its Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth.
Discovery 5. Its Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth.
Jupiter also has faint rings made of tiny dark particles.
Discovery 6. Jupiter also has faint rings made of tiny dark particles.
Correct. A giant storm.
Saturn. The ringed planet. Tilt the view and inspect Saturn’s icy rings.
Rings are made of ice and rock chunks.
Discovery 1. Rings are made of ice and rock chunks.
Has lots of moons to discover.
Discovery 2. Has lots of moons to discover.
Could float in water because it is light.
Discovery 3. Could float in water because it is light.
Spins so fast it looks squished.
Discovery 4. Spins so fast it looks squished.
Some ring pieces are tiny grains; others are house-sized.
Discovery 5. Some ring pieces are tiny grains; others are house-sized.
Titan is one of Saturn’s moons. It is so cold that methane, a gas on Earth, falls there as rain and fills lakes.
Discovery 6. Titan is one of Saturn’s moons. It is so cold that methane, a gas on Earth, falls there as rain and fills lakes.
Correct. Ice and rock.
Uranus. The sideways spinner. Find the pale planet rolling around the Sun on its side.
Spins on its side like a rolling ball.
Discovery 1. Spins on its side like a rolling ball.
Pale blue-green color from methane gas.
Discovery 2. Pale blue-green color from methane gas.
Very cold and far from the Sun.
Discovery 3. Very cold and far from the Sun.
Has faint rings around it.
Discovery 4. Has faint rings around it.
Its seasons each last about 21 Earth years.
Discovery 5. Its seasons each last about 21 Earth years.
Scientists think it may rain diamonds deep inside.
Discovery 6. Scientists think it may rain diamonds deep inside.
Correct. On its side.
Neptune. The windy blue world. Travel to the far blue world and look for storm bands.
Farthest planet from the Sun.
Discovery 1. Farthest planet from the Sun.
Super windy with giant storms.
Discovery 2. Super windy with giant storms.
Methane gas helps give Neptune its blue colour.
Discovery 3. Methane gas helps give Neptune its blue colour.
A year there is very, very long.
Discovery 4. A year there is very, very long.
Its winds can race faster than 2,000 kilometres per hour.
Discovery 5. Its winds can race faster than 2,000 kilometres per hour.
Triton is a moon of Neptune. It goes around Neptune in the direction opposite to the way Neptune spins.
Discovery 6. Triton is a moon of Neptune. It goes around Neptune in the direction opposite to the way Neptune spins.
Correct. Super-fast winds.
Pluto. The tiny icy dwarf planet. Find the tiny icy world beyond Neptune.
Small, icy world far from the Sun.
Discovery 1. Small, icy world far from the Sun.
Used to be called the 9th planet.
Discovery 2. Used to be called the 9th planet.
Has a heart-shaped ice spot.
Discovery 3. Has a heart-shaped ice spot.
Takes 248 years to go around the Sun.
Discovery 4. Takes 248 years to go around the Sun.
Its heart-shaped region is called Tombaugh Regio.
Discovery 5. Its heart-shaped region is called Tombaugh Regio.
Charon is Pluto’s largest moon. Pluto and Charon travel around one point between them. This point is their shared centre of gravity.
Discovery 6. Charon is Pluto’s largest moon. Pluto and Charon travel around one point between them. This point is their shared centre of gravity.
Correct. A dwarf planet.
Not quite. Check the discoveries and try again.
